description: Nuestro equipo enfocará el aprendizaje interactivo mediante las historias de los objetos y equipos que la NASA ha dejado en la Luna y Marte. Utilizando mapas, fotografías y relatos, permite explorar su origen, función y legado, acercando al público la historia de la exploración espacial y recordándonos que cada misión deja una huella en el universo
summary:
Astro-Reliquias is a web-based educational gamification platform developed for NASA's "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. Its primary objective is to reframe discarded lunar and Martian equipment as historical technological heritage rather than space debris.  
The system architecture utilizes a lightweight frontend stack comprising HTML5, SVG, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript, integrated with HTML5 Canvas and Web Audio APIs for fluid interactive rendering. The application implements a three-tier pedagogical matrix: a Knowledge Phase utilizing synthesized metadata cards for eight space modules and rovers, a Spatial Application Phase employing drag-and-drop celestial mapping to the Moon or Mars with heuristic feedback loops, and a Reflection Phase fostering critical thinking on technology repurposing.  
Furthermore, the development workflow integrated Google Gemini AI for parsing dense public mission datasets into accessible pedagogical formats and optimizing algorithmic logic. Ultimately, the platform empowers youth demographics to engage with NASA's historical milestones while conceptualizing sustainable frameworks for future space exploration.
details:
Astro-Relics is an interactive, educational game developed for the NASA challenge, "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars." Aimed at the general public—with a focus on young people and students aged 16 and under—the project uses accessible language to shift perceptions regarding equipment left behind in space. It teaches that these items are not mere "space junk," but rather historical heritage and technological relics that remain on the Moon or Mars for valid reasons (such as weight limits for return journeys, design as passive stations, or the completion of their operational lifespan).

Game Structure and Mechanics

The educational experience is divided into three progressive stages designed to foster knowledge acquisition, practical application, and critical thinking:

Stage 1: Knowledge Phase (Exploring Heritage)

Players explore eight visual, illustrated profiles of various pieces of historical equipment left in space:

• On the Moon: The Eagle lunar module (Apollo 11), the Lunar Roving Vehicle (Apollo 15), the Surveyor 3 probe, and the Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector.

• On Mars: The Opportunity rover, the Spirit rover, the InSight lander, and the Sojourner rover.

Each profile organizes its content into five thematic categories to help users understand the item's historical significance:

Thematic Category Description and Purpose

Mission and Origin Identifies the mission name (e.g., Apollo 11, Mars Pathfinder) and the year it arrived in space.

Function Explains the equipment’s purpose in simple terms (e.g., measuring seismic activity, analyzing rocks, or transporting astronauts).

Reason for Remaining (Key category) Provides the technical justification for why the equipment was left behind, dispelling the notion of negligent abandonment.

Legacy Highlights the scientific or historical impact achieved (e.g., confirming the presence of water on Mars or enabling human exploration on the Moon). Fun Fact: Presents a striking detail to capture the interest of young people (e.g., the Opportunity rover operated for 15 years instead of the planned 90 days).

Stage 2: Placement Phase (Space Application)

The player tests what they have learned using an interactive map that splits the screen between the surfaces of the Moon and Mars:

• Mechanic: The player must drag each "Astro-Relic" to the celestial body where it is located.

• Non-punitive feedback: There is no "Game Over"; if the user makes a mistake, the system provides an educational, context-specific hint (for example, noting that the Eagle module carried humans to the celestial body closest to Earth) to encourage another attempt.

Stage 3: Reflection Phase (Innovation and the Future)

To complete the game 100%, the user must take an active role by answering a hypothetical question: "If you were the director of NASA and had the final say, would you assign a new purpose to any of the objects or pieces of equipment mentioned?" The goal is to stimulate the creativity of young people, encouraging them to imagine future uses for these technologies—such as repurposing old rovers as topographical markers, historical monuments, or shelters made from existing materials.

Impact and Objectives Achieved

The development of "Astro-Relics" accomplishes three key goals in science outreach:

• Shifting the narrative: It replaces a negative view—"trash" or "abandonment"—with an appreciation for these items as technological heritage and relics.

• Active education: It facilitates the retention of NASA’s space history through gamification and a trial-and-error learning process, free from penalties.

• Inspiring youth: It empowers students by validating their ideas for reimagining technological sustainability and the future of space exploration.
